input.stem:
Iron exhibits allotropy and exists in two distinct cubic crystalline forms: α-iron, where iron atoms occupy all the corners and the body centre of the cubic unit cell, and γ-iron, where iron atoms occupy all the corners and the centres of all faces of the cubic unit cell. At specific temperatures, the measured density of α-iron is 7.899 g cm^-3, whereas the density of γ-iron is 8.004 g cm^-3. Determine the difference in the atomic radius of iron (in pm) between γ-iron and α-iron, defined as (r_γ - r_α).
(Given: Molar mass of iron, Fe = 55.85 g mol^-1; Avogadro's constant, N_A = 6.022 × 10^23 mol^-1) Give the answer in pm, to 3 significant figures.
